topology: NMOS differential pair, two NMOS cascodes, cascoded PMOS mirror load, NMOS tail plus explicit diode-connected bias reference
OP_interpretation: The AC fixture closes external negative feedback at DC through an inductor and opens it at AC. The declared0.7..1.2V window accepts a headroom-valid operating point; it is not a claim of intrinsic CMFB, precision tracking, or continuous usable swing across that entire interval. Each actual MOS must additionally pass the explicit channel-voltage and saturation checks.
power_accounting: Total DC power is P_VDD+P_VBN+P_VBP, from actual source currents. IREF is connected from VDD into IBIAS; its entire VDD*10u reference branch is already included in P_VDD. Report (VDD-Vbias)*10u for the ideal current-source dissipation and Vbias*10u for its reference MOS as components, without adding them again. Input stimulus driver power is outside the quiescent circuit budget. VBN/VBP are ideal external voltage-bias ports. Their actual source output power is included, while the implementation overhead of an on-chip bias generator is outside this fixture; no zero-overhead bias-generator claim is made.
electrical_basis: The two cascode stacks increase output resistance; the output load supplies the dominant pole. Upper PMOS gates sense the lower left collector across the entire reference stack, allowing external VBP to set cascode-source headroom without fixing the mirror input transistor's drain to its gate. VBN covers nominal lower-stack headroom; VBP covers upper-stack headroom. These are design hypotheses, not observed operation or a stability guarantee.

source_ancestry.independence_limit: High-level topology and assembly logic are new; basic primitive/access constraints are shared. This is not a claim of zero source dependency overlap.

selection_rule: Measure all four fixed controls at all three corners once. If any passes every declared OP/AC requirement, the first in the declared order is the prospective physical-control bias. Do not search further if none passes. A passing ideal OP/AC control does not establish DRC, LVS, positive RC, transient/DC correctness or S2.
